voyage.name: Auckland Art Gallery
voyage.price: Free entry for New Zealand residents, for international adults $20; charges for some special exhibitions
voyage.content: The largest collection of national and international art in New Zealand, housed in a landmark building on the edge of Albert Park in the heart of Auckland. Regularly hosts touring international exhibitions and offers a calendar of talks, performances, film screenings and children's activities to complement its exhibition programme. Has a shop and café.

voyage.name: Auckland Domain
voyage.content: A large park (75 ha) on an extinct volcano. It has the War Memorial Museum on its highest point and also the historically important winter gardens with impressive flower bed displays, tropical plants and statues (free). There are scenic views of the Waitemata Harbour and islands of the Hauraki Gulf from in front of the museum.

voyage.name: Auckland War Memorial Museum
voyage.price: Overseas adult $25, overseas child 6-14 years $10; NZ residents donation invited; Auckland residents free with MyMuseum card or proof of residency
voyage.content: Despite the name, this is not primarily a war museum – it is a general museum and one of the best in New Zealand. It stands in an imposing position in Auckland Domain. It includes excellent displays of Māori and other Polynesian peoples' arts and crafts, the geography of the Auckland region, and daily Māori cultural performances (ground floor). The top floor records names in stone, sobering tombs and lists of war eve

voyage.name: Auckland Zoo
voyage.price: Adults (15 years+) $28, children 4–14 $12, seniors and students with ID $23, family rates available
voyage.hours: 1 Sep-30 Apr 9:30AM–5:30PM (last admissions at 16:15), but Fridays open until 8PM; 1 May–31 Aug 9:30AM-5PM; closed 25 Dec
voyage.content: The zoo has the largest collection of native and exotic animals in New Zealand, with 120 animal species, over 750 animals and a number of different habitats such as the Rainforest and Pridelands (an African savannah) set in 17 hectares.

voyage.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral
voyage.content: Large modern Anglican cathedral that opened in 1965 and can seat 1100 people. Next to it is St Mary's Church, the largest wooden Gothic church in the world, built in 1886 and moved to the present site in 1982.

voyage.name: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium
voyage.content: It's on the scenic Tamaki Drive and is the home of Antarctic Encounter and Underwater World. It includes a trip through a transparent tunnel while the fish and sharks swim all around you, and tanks of rays with feeding-time talks.

voyage.name: The Lighthouse / Tū Whenua-a-Kura
voyage.content: A sculpture by Michael Parekowhai in the form of a 1950s house, which sits on the end of the wharf. You can't enter the house, but you can look in the windows at the lighting display inspired by the southern skies and a stainless steel sculpture of Captain James Cook. The artwork was installed in 2017. It can be viewed any time, but it may be best to avoid days when cruise ships are alongside.

voyage.name: MOTAT (Museum of Transport and Technology)
voyage.hours: Daily 10AM-5PM, closed for one week in March
voyage.content: An interactive technology museum with over 300,000 items, divided among two campuses: one showcasing aviation artifacts, and the other (larger) one on general science and technology, with a focus on communications (history of the telegraph, for example) and transportation. Look out for the WWII Avro Lancaster Bomber and the Solent Flying Boat in the Sir Keith Park Memorial Aviation Collection.

voyage.name: Mount Eden / Maungawhau
voyage.content: The highest natural point in Auckland at 196 m above sea level, this volcanic peak provides 360-degree views from beside the 50-metre deep crater at its summit. There are numerous pedestrian entrances from surrounding streets to the hill's walkways.

voyage.name: New Zealand Maritime Museum
voyage.address: corner Quay and Hobson Sts, Viaduct Harbour
voyage.content: Many interesting exhibits chronicle New Zealand's maritime history, including actual yachts from the America's Cup and interactive displays and machines. There is an Auckland harbour cruise on an old-style cargo scow that takes about 1 hour and costs extra (adult $25). You can also see the "ship in a bottle" exhibit, and meet the volunteers working on the models.

voyage.name: One Tree Hill / Maungakiekie
voyage.content: The second highest peak in the city at 182 m above sea level, this volcanic cone offers panoramic views of the city. An obelisk on the summit marks the grave of Sir John Logan Campbell, a founding father of Auckland city. The summit has not had a solitary tree, for which it was known, since 2000. Terraces where the structures of a fortified Maori village (pa) once stood are still visible on the slopes. The peak is su

voyage.name: Sky Tower
voyage.hours: Daily 9:30AM–8PM (last entry 7:15PM), later Fri and Sat, and Dec-Jan
voyage.content: At 328 m, this is the tallest free-standing tower in the Southern Hemisphere, offering views of up to 80 km away and fine dining in the Orbit revolving restaurant.

voyage.name: St Matthew's Church
voyage.hours: usually open Mon-Fri 10 AM - 4.30PM, Services Sun 8AM, 10AM, Wed 12:20PM
voyage.content: Anglican church. The fine neo-Gothic stone church building opened in 1905.

voyage.name: Stardome Observatory & Planetarium
voyage.address: 670 Manukau Rd, One Tree Hill Domain

voyage.name: St Patrick's Roman Catholic Cathedral
voyage.alt: Cathedral of Saint Patrick and Saint Joseph
voyage.hours: Masses daily, 4 on Sun, often open for viewing midweek.
voyage.address: Corner of Federal St and Wyndham St
voyage.content: Busy catholic cathedral which can have 3000 attend one of the 4 masses on a Sunday. The foundation stone of this traditional stone building was laid in 1884, on a site granted by the Crown in 1841.

voyage.name: Silo Park
voyage.address: Corner of Jellicoe Street and Beaumont Street, Wynyard Quarter
voyage.content: A waterfront public space built around former industrial silos, with public art, a playground, basketball facilities and seasonal events.

voyage.name: Aotea Square
voyage.content: A large central public square beside Auckland Town Hall and Aotea Centre, used for festivals, markets, performances and civic events.

voyage.name: Te Komititanga
voyage.content: A public square outside Waitematā Station. Its basalt paving forms a whāriki, or welcome mat, and the space is used for events and civic gatherings.

voyage.name: Auckland Town Hall
voyage.content: A civic and performance building opened in 1911, containing the Great Hall, Concert Chamber and a large pipe organ.

voyage.name: The Civic
voyage.address: Corner of Queen Street and Wellesley Street
voyage.content: A 1929 atmospheric theatre with a Moorish-style auditorium, a starry ceiling and the smaller Wintergarden performance space.

voyage.name: Alberton
voyage.address: 100 Mt Albert Rd, Mt Albert (entrance from Kerr-Taylor Ave)
voyage.content: An 18-room mansion started in 1863. It was the centre of social life for its area during the late 19th century.

voyage.name: Ewelme Cottage
voyage.content: Built in 1863–64 as a home for a vicar's family. Much smaller than Alberton and Highwic. Well preserved interior showing middle class family accommodation in the late nineteenth century.

voyage.name: Kinder House
voyage.address: Corner of Parnell Road and Ayr Street, Parnell
voyage.content: House built in 1857 for John Kinder (1819 – 1903), the headmaster of a nearby Church of England School. A couple of rooms are used for exhibitions, but the interior has not been preserved.

voyage.name: Highwic
voyage.content: Home for a very large family (21 children, although the older ones would have left before the youngest was born) built from 1862.

voyage.name: Arts House Trust / Pah Homestead
voyage.content: An art gallery with a very substantial collection in a mansion built 1877-79. A collection of New Zealand art is displayed as the Arts Centre. The large Monte Cecilia Park surrounds the house and was once its grounds.

voyage.name: Auckland Bridge Climb
voyage.price: Adult $130, child $90, check for promotional discounts
voyage.content: If you have a head for heights, you can walk up the arch of the Harbour Bridge. Bungy jumps from the bridge are also available.

voyage.name: Auckland Sea Kayaks
voyage.address: St Heliers Central Boat Ramp, 384 Tamaki Dr
voyage.content: Sea kayaking tours including to the islands of Rangitoto, Motutapu, Motuihe and Motukorea (Browns Island). Auckland is a unique sea kayaking location. Tours suitable for all experience levels. Tours launch at St Heliers - free pickup from downtown.

voyage.name: Auckland Whale & Dolphin Safari
voyage.content: Explore the beautiful Hauraki Gulf Marine Park during a 4.5-hour marine eco-safari on a purpose-built vessel, the Dolphin Explorer. They have years of experience and guarantee that you will see marine mammals – or your next trip is free.

voyage.name: Eden Park
voyage.content: New Zealand's top sports stadium, hosting cricket in summer and rugby union in winter - the All Blacks national rugby team often play here. In 2023 it staged matches in the Women's World Cup for soccer, co-hosted by NZ and Australia. Event tickets often include free train travel to and from the park – get off the train at Kingsland not Mount Eden Station.

voyage.name: Explore NZ
voyage.content: Waitemata Harbour sailboat cruises on a boat from the Pride of Auckland fleet. Also offer a 2-hr Sailing Experience on an original America's Cup yacht. Other activities are available.

voyage.name: Manukau coastal walks between Onehunga and Blockhouse Bay
voyage.content: The track is 9 km long in total, but meets the roads in many places, so you can easily do just part of it. It includes areas of native forest.

voyage.name: Odyssey Sensory Maze
voyage.content: Indoor maze with several rooms, each with a unique theme, and allowing for a different sensory experience: guess the smell/sound/object (by touch); find your way out of a room full of mirrors; swim through a balloon pit etc.

voyage.name: Rangitoto Island
voyage.content: A dormant volcano island that stands prominently near the entrance to the Waitemata Harbour. Climb to the summit for fantastic views of the harbour and Auckland city. Take a picnic or have a swim. There is a guided tour that will take you most of the way up the volcano (on a very bumpy road in a tractor trailer) for about $30. There are no shops on the island, so buy any food and drink you need before you go. Toilets

voyage.name: Sky Jump
voyage.content: A cable-controlled base jump from a height of 192 m on the Sky Tower. Also the Sky Walk, a walk around a 1.2 m walkway with no hand rails.

voyage.name: Wynyard Loop tram
voyage.content: A short tram loop, run by MOTAT. Operating hours and length of loop in operation depend on the redevelopment in progress in the area. Two vintage trams are used on this route.

voyage.name: Franklin Road Christmas Lights
voyage.content: Every year the residents of this street put up a stunning display of lights on their houses. The street has many early 20th century houses tightly packed together. The display can be seen by driving along Franklin Road, but this is clogged with traffic on these nights and the display is best seen on foot. On some evening buskers and choirs are outside a few houses.

voyage.name: Wētā Workshop Unleashed
voyage.content: A guided, interactive attraction exploring practical film effects through original horror, science-fiction and fantasy sets created by Wētā Workshop.

voyage.name: Aotea Centre
voyage.content: A performing-arts and events centre on Aotea Square containing the Kiri Te Kanawa Theatre, Herald Theatre and exhibition and function spaces.

voyage.name: All Blacks Experience
voyage.content: A guided interactive attraction about New Zealand rugby, covering the All Blacks and Black Ferns, Māori culture, the haka and rugby skills activities.

voyage.name: Albert Park
voyage.content: A CBD park laid out in the 1880s, with flower gardens, specimen trees, a floral clock, sculptures, artworks and two field guns from 1879.

voyage.name: Myers Park
voyage.content: A park that can be used as route between Queen St and K Rd (passing through St Kevin's Arcade). Has a children's playground.

voyage.name: Kiwa Art
voyage.content: High-end quality Maori and Polynesian art. Collaborates with local designers, artisans, jewelers and carvers and covers the whole price range for greenstone and other Polynesian art.

voyage.name: Victoria Park Market
voyage.content: It used to have lots of craft stalls, then was renovated and reopened in 2013.

voyage.name: The Warehouse
voyage.content: Value chain store for household goods, clothing and a small selection of food.

voyage.name: Westfield Newmarket
voyage.content: Large 3-floor shopping mall, which opened in 2019 with David Jones and Farmers department stores and a Woolworths supermarket.

voyage.name: The Women's Bookshop
voyage.content: Not exclusively books by women writers, but those are clearly the focus, and the staff are friendly and knowledgeable. The shop is relatively small but has an interesting selection, including sizeable sections focused on writers from New Zealand and LGBTQI+ books.

voyage.name: Commercial Bay
voyage.content: A downtown shopping and dining precinct with fashion, beauty and specialty shops as well as a large food and restaurant area.

voyage.name: Auckland Fish Market
voyage.content: A seafood market and food hall with a retail fishmonger and several eateries serving seafood and other takeaway and dine-in food.

voyage.name: Woolworths Auckland Metro
voyage.content: Small central supermarket.

voyage.name: New World Metro Queen Street
voyage.content: Small central supermarket.

voyage.name: New World Victoria Park
voyage.content: Badly damaged by a fire in June 2025, closed until 2027 for repairs.

voyage.name: Lim Chhour
voyage.content: The only supermarket on Karangahape Road. Asian Supermarket.

voyage.name: Furein Asian Supermarket
voyage.content: Large central Asian supermarket.

voyage.name: Tart Bakery
voyage.content: Plant-based bakery with a variety of "you wouldn't know it's vegan" pastries.

voyage.name: Little Algiers
voyage.content: Very good value for money. North African cuisine.

voyage.name: Burger Fuel
voyage.address: many locations, including Parnell Rd, and Dominion Rd (Mt Eden)
voyage.content: Delicious gourmet burgers. Vegetarian and vegan options available.

voyage.name: Fatimas
voyage.address: 7 Queen St, 240 Ponsonby Rd in Ponsonby; and 20 Anzac St in Takapuna
voyage.content: Excellent kebabs and pitas, a step above typical post-clubbing fare.

voyage.name: Ima Cuisine
voyage.content: Levantine meals from an Israeli chef.

voyage.name: Mezze Bar
voyage.content: Serves tapas and other dishes. Often busy but worth the wait.

voyage.name: Nishiki, Robata-Yaki Bar
voyage.content: Great Japanese restaurant. Requires reservation for all days of the week. Great value for money.

voyage.name: East Restaurant
voyage.content: Elegant, flavourful Asian fusion with an emphasis on plant-based dishes.

voyage.name: One Tree Grill Restaurant
voyage.content: An Epsom restaurant serving modern New Zealand and European cuisine with a seasonal menu and a large wine selection. Established in 1996. Selected for the 2026 Michelin Guide.

voyage.name: The Occidental
voyage.content: A popular place with the after-work crowd. Serves traditional Belgian beers alongside Belgian cuisine, including mussels and frites.

voyage.name: Shadows Bar
voyage.content: Student bar with decent prices.

voyage.name: Cassette Number 9
voyage.content: A bar and club featuring different music nights.

voyage.name: SkyCity
voyage.content: Entertainment complex with a dozen bars & cafes including Bellota, a Spanish tapas bar.

voyage.name: The Brit
voyage.price: Mains $17-30, beer starts at $5 for a can of Lion Brown
voyage.content: Gastropub.

voyage.name: Galbraiths Alehouse
voyage.content: A brewery and pub with a great selection of traditional beer and wine.

voyage.name: Small Gods
voyage.content: Hole-in-the-wall brewery - gem of craft beer making old recipes and modern drinks. Beer sold in pints, cans and flagons.

voyage.name: Churly's
voyage.content: A brewery serving beer from Behemoth Brewing Co. Small plates of food available but can be fairly expensive.

voyage.name: Garage Project Cellar Door
voyage.content: Smallish "cellar door" style, serving tasting flights of 6 or so beers. You can select your beers or let the staff choose for you.

voyage.name: Urbanaut
voyage.content: A brewery and bar serving craft beer and cider. Food is available.

voyage.name: The Beer Spot Morningside
voyage.content: A bar with a large rotating selection of craft beers. There is a food truck which changes weekly.

voyage.name: Brothers Brewing
voyage.content: Serving beer from Brothers brewery and food to share.

voyage.name: Haka House Auckland City
voyage.content: Has dorms with up to 10 beds and private rooms. Now run by the Haka House, having been previously owned by the YHA. They have another hostel nearby on Karangahape Road.

voyage.name: BK Hostel
voyage.content: Just 4 beds in the dorm rooms. Nice atmosphere, kitchen and laundry.

voyage.name: Choice Backpackers
voyage.content: Easygoing, friendly, cheap.

voyage.name: Edit Auckland Central
voyage.content: Budget hotel with reliable wifi, a small gym, laundry room, and breakfast included. Luggage storage available.

voyage.name: City Lodge Auckland
voyage.content: Run by the YMCA, this is half-way between a hostel and a hotel. All the rooms (singles, doubles and triples) are ensuite with a fridge and TV, but are a little basic compared to a hotel. There is a laundry, large shared kitchen and lounge on the ground floor. The YMCA also have a hostel nearby with dormitories and single/double rooms.

voyage.name: Rendevous Heritage Auckland
voyage.content: Four-star plus hotel with restaurant and bar. Serviced apartments available.

voyage.name: Quest Auckland
voyage.content: Close to Aotea Centre, the Town Hall, restaurants and shopping. 70 studios, one and two-bedroom serviced apartments all with kitchen and laundry facilities. One of a number in the Quest Serviced Apartments chain in Auckland.

voyage.name: Grand Millennium
voyage.content: A grand 4-star plus hotel built in 1989 with 452 guest rooms and suites, a bar, Straits Cafe, and Katsura Japanese restaurant. The lower-priced rooms when discounted are very reasonably priced for a hotel of its rating.

voyage.name: Auckland Waterfront Apartments
voyage.content: Luxury 1-, 2- & 3-bedroom serviced apartments with harbour views.

voyage.name: Braemar
voyage.content: Beautifully renovated 1901 Edwardian townhouse.

voyage.name: Cordis, Auckland
voyage.content: Five-star luxury hotel, formerly called the Langham.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Auckland
voyage.content: Four-star plus hotel with 352 guest rooms and suites.

voyage.name: Hilton Auckland
voyage.content: A modern waterfront building with great views over the harbour. Quite close to the ferry terminals and a short walk to the Wynyard area.

voyage.name: Pullman Auckland
voyage.content: Five-star hotel in the CBD with 340 rooms and self-contained apartments, free Wi-Fi, health club and spa, restaurant.

voyage.name: Sebel Auckland Viaduct Harbour
voyage.content: Apartment hotel in the business and dining precinct at Viaduct Harbour.

voyage.name: Sebel Quay West Auckland
voyage.content: A luxury apartment hotel in the CBD featuring balconies with harbour & city views.

voyage.name: Skycity Grand Hotel
voyage.content: Five-star luxury hotel.

voyage.name: Chelsea Bay
voyage.content: Visitor centre and one-hour guided tours of the Chelsea Sugar Refinery. Also has a bakery and cafe for some sugary goodies. Opened Oct 2018.

voyage.name: Long Bay Regional Park
voyage.content: Stroll around the park and along the beach and enjoy the views over the Hauraki Gulf and adjoining marine reserve. There are also walks, sea kayaking, picnic areas, the historic Vaughan homestead and a kid's playground that has a miniature train.

voyage.name: Harbourside Art Trail
voyage.content: Take your time and visit the studios of the local artists and craftspeople in Birkenhead and Northcote.

voyage.name: Movies
voyage.content: It has cheap ticket prices: adult tickets at $10.90. Events Cinemas at Albany charges $18.50, the usual Auckland price, while at Hoyts Wairau Park they are $19.50, the highest price in Auckland – both these places have a Tuesday special of $12.50. (in 2017).

voyage.name: North Head
voyage.content: Take a stroll around. It's in Devonport at the mouth of the Waitemata Harbour. It has stunning views over the Hauraki Gulf and inner harbour. Look out for the complex of tunnels, guns and other fortifications. Spending a day exploring the tunnels and having a picnic is strongly advised. North Head offers spectacular views of North Shore, central Auckland, the harbour bridge and the volcanic island of Rangitoto.

voyage.name: Snowplanet
voyage.content: New Zealand's only indoor ski resort.

voyage.name: Walk the North Shore section of Te Araroa Trail
voyage.content: A 23-km coastal walking route from Long Bay to Devonport, part of Te Araroa, which runs the length of New Zealand.

voyage.name: Bushman's Grill
voyage.hours: Dinner daily from 5:30PM, lunch Fri Sun noon-2PM
voyage.content: Steak house.

voyage.name: Quest Albany
voyage.content: Air-conditioned apartment accommodation with free Wi-Fi and unlimited data.

voyage.name: Auckland Botanic Gardens
voyage.content: Over 10,000 different plant types, both natives and exotics, spread over 64 hectares.

voyage.name: Butterfly Creek
voyage.content: A tropical butterfly and moth house. Any time is good to see the butterflies but the best time is on sunny mornings. The butterfly house is warm and humid. Also has a few crocodiles and alligators, tamarin monkeys, dinosaur display, tropical aquaria, farmyard animals, a train for the kids and a cafe.

voyage.name: Howick Historical Village
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun, except 1 Jan, 25 & 26 Dec, Good Fri and Anzac Day 10AM-4PM
voyage.address: corner of Lady Marie Dr & Bells Rd, Lloyd Elsmore Park, Pakuranga
voyage.content: This historical park gives visitors a taste of what life was like from 1840 to 1880.

voyage.name: Maraetai Beach
voyage.content: Popular local beach for the Southern and Eastern suburbs. The road to Maraetai beach and around the Maraetai Coast Road is popular for driving and motorcycles.

voyage.name: Otuataua Stonefields
voyage.content: Site of ancient Maori gardens on a low volcano.

voyage.name: Papakura Museum
voyage.content: Museum run by Papakura & Districts Historical Society.

voyage.name: McNicol Homestead
voyage.content: 1878 house set in grounds with a museum run by the local historical society. Refurbished in 2025

voyage.name: Rainbow's End
voyage.address: 2 Clist Cres, off Manukau Station Rd, Manukau Central
voyage.content: NZ’s premier family-based theme park with many rides and attractions.

voyage.name: Mangere Mountain
voyage.content: An extinct volcano and former site of a pre-European Maori village, overlooking the Manukau Harbour.

voyage.name: Glenbrook Vintage Railway
voyage.hours: Runs on many summer Sundays and some occasional other days
voyage.content: 7-km steam railway.

voyage.name: Mangere Town Centre market
voyage.content: Similar to Otara Flea Market. A good place to buy Polynesian food.

voyage.name: The Hangi Shop
voyage.content: Restaurant serving traditional Māori food including Hangi, a meal cooked by rocks in an underground pit.

voyage.name: Airport Skyway Lodge
voyage.content: Comfortable airport transfer service and very friendly staff. Car hire possible.

voyage.name: Heartland Hotel Auckland Airport
voyage.content: Close to the airport.

voyage.name: Kudos Airport Apartments
voyage.address: Unit 40 Kudos Business Centre, 203 Kirkbride Rd, Mangere
voyage.content: Twelve serviced apartment suites with 2 bedrooms, fully equipped kitchen and laundry facilities.

voyage.name: Arataki Visitor Centre
voyage.hours: Visitor Centre daily 10AM-4PM, Sat, Sun & summer 9AM-5PM; park open 6AM-6PM in winter, 6AM-9PM in summer
voyage.content: An attraction popular with tour groups. Around the centre there are nature trails which signpost the native trees and birds found in the area. Trails range from 10 minutes to 4-5 hours and are all fully maintained and signposted. The centre itself features models, history and facts of native birds and the surrounding area. The view from Scenic Drive is amazing, the west coast one side and the city the other.

voyage.name: McCahon House
voyage.address: 67 Otitori Bay Road, French Bay, Titirangi
voyage.content: The former home (and garden) of a famous 20th century New Zealand painter, Colin McCahon.

voyage.name: West Wave Pool and Leisure Centre
voyage.content: If the weather is not so go for a swim. Home of the 1992 Commonwealth Games competition pools, they have been though major expansion and renovation over the past 3 years. Now the complex consists of 2 x 50m 8 lane pools, a drive pool with 9 boards, a hydroslide, 2 toddlers pools, spa, sauna, steam room facilities, a lazy river and a wave pool. There is also an onsite gym and a cafe.

voyage.name: Event Cinemas WestCity
voyage.address: Level 4, Westfield Westcity, Edsel St, Henderson

voyage.name: Event Cinemas Westgate
voyage.address: Westgate Shopping Centre 1-5 Fernhill Dr, Massey

voyage.name: Skydive Auckland
voyage.content: Imagine an insanity inducing freefall of at least 200kmph with breathtaking views of the skies and beaches of Auckland. Skydive heights of 9,000, 13,000 & 16,500ft are used, the last of which is the highest skydive jump in the North Island.

voyage.name: Musashi
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant.

voyage.name: New Haven Motel
voyage.content: hotel with cooking facilities and swimming pool

voyage.name: Heritage Collection Waitakere Estate
voyage.content: Luxury hotel and restaurant.
